skills.name: Portuguese Africa: delayed decolonisation and varied transitions

note.text: Portugal retained its African empire while many other colonies became independent. Its authoritarian government defended continued control, and liberation movements fought protracted wars in Angola, Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau. Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde and São Tomé and Príncipe followed distinct routes. Portugal’s April revolution in 1974 changed the metropolitan political framework and opened negotiations. Guinea-Bissau declared independence in 1973 and gained Portuguese recognition in 1974; Mozambique, Cape Verde, São Tomé and Príncipe and Angola became independent in 1975. Declaration and recognition must be distinguished.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to identify the territories and connect liberation struggles with the change of regime in Portugal. Builds on: British, French and Belgian transitions. Leads to: post-independence instability and comparative explanations.

sections.heading: Explain the history
sections.text: Portugal retained its African empire while many other colonies became independent. Its authoritarian government defended continued control, and liberation movements fought protracted wars in Angola, Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau. Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde and São Tomé and Príncipe followed distinct routes. Portugal’s April revolution in {1974} changed the metropolitan political framework and opened negotiations. Guinea-Bissau declared independence in {1973} and gained Portuguese recognition in {1974}; Mozambique, Cape Verde, São Tomé and Príncipe and Angola became independent in {1975}. Declaration and recognition must be distinguished.

sections.heading: Follow the evidence and examples
sections.text: Examples of movements include FRELIMO in Mozambique, PAIGC in Guinea-Bissau/Cape Verde, and rival movements including MPLA, FNLA and UNITA in Angola. The {1974} revolution did not erase earlier African resistance or guarantee peaceful transitions everywhere. Angola’s continuing conflict illustrates why independence and lasting peace are separate questions.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Identify actor, action, place and period before explaining a relationship. Use the practice text only for the claim it supports. Distinguish a cause, an event and an outcome; compare authentic sources before treating an interpretation as established. A sequence alone does not prove that every later outcome was inevitable.

key_words.meaning: Portugal’s prolonged defence of its African empire
African organisations pursuing independence through political and armed struggle
the change in Portugal enabling a new decolonisation policy
the difference between declaration, recognition and later political outcomes

cards.idea: Connect a specific action or event to the historical feature it illustrates.
example: The authoritarian Portuguese regime resisted independence while wars developed in several territories.
FRELIMO organised the independence struggle in Mozambique.
The April {1974} revolution opened a different political route to negotiation.

cards.idea: Check a claim against the sequence, setting and limits of the evidence.
example: Every Portuguese territory followed Ghana’s peaceful constitutional timetable. Correction: The regimes and routes differed.
African resistance began only after Portugal had already transferred all power. Correction: Movements and struggles preceded the final transfers.
The revolution made earlier African resistance irrelevant. Correction: Metropolitan change interacted with prior struggles and pressure.
Declaration and Portuguese recognition necessarily occurred in the same year everywhere. Correction: The Guinean sequence shows distinct stages.
